newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar likely to be range-bound in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar likely to be range-bound in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to trade in a narrow range against the yen and the mark in Asia on Friday, as a long weekend in the United States is expected to curtail activity.

The dollar could find support at around 113.30 yen as Japanese institutional investors are expected to show buying interest near 113 yen, but its upside is expected to be heavy at around 114 yen, they said.
"Some Japanese investors could also sell dollars on its recovery for hedging purposes. So this could make the dollar's topside heavy," said a city bank trader.

The dollar fell against other major currencies on Thursday in New York as expectations of a near-term increase in U.S. interest rates faded after the U.S. employment report showed an uptick in the unemployment rate to 5.0 percent in June from 4.8 percent in May.
There was talk that some Japanese life insurers sold dollars in a large lot after the U.S. jobs data was released, traders said.
Meanwhile, the dollar's overnight fall versus the mark was less steep partly due to the German currency's weakness against the yen and the British pound.

"The dollar also dipped versus the mark after the U.S. employment report, but dollar/mark bids were quite solid. Sterling's strength against the mark could continue to help support dollar/mark," said the city bank trader.

In New York, the pound rose to its highest level in almost six years against the mark and surged to a high of $1.6929, its top level since early January, before settling at $1.6910/20, up from $1.6755/65 at the open.
The pound's strength is likely to continue as market participants are expecting an interest rate hike from the Bank of England as early as next week, a trust bank trader said.
Traders said the mark is also likely to remain under pressure versus the yen as Japanese exporters are falling behind schedule in selling marks for the yen.
The dollar closed at 113.58/68 yen and 1.7512/22 marks in New York on Thursday.
The mark stood at around 64.87 yen in late Thursday in New York.
